analysis.title: GS US Daily Download 5 Oct 2026
key_insights: Hedge funds rotated into TMT stocks in September while nearly every other sector was net sold.
Q3 2026 earnings season starts the week of October 12. About 70% of S&P 500 market cap will have reported by the end of October, and most hyperscalers report in the last week of October.
Consensus expects S&P 500 y/y EPS growth of 27% in Q3, versus realized growth of 33% in Q2 excluding some accounting distortions.
Beneficiaries of AI infrastructure spending account for over 50% of S&P 500 EPS growth this quarter in analyst estimates, alongside hyperscaler capex growth of 116%.
GS expects most companies to beat consensus earnings estimates again in Q3.
For the median S&P 500 stock, consensus y/y EPS growth slows from 14% in Q2 to 9% in Q3.

Input cost pressures likely limit sequential margin expansion in Q3, and the dollar is a modestly smaller tailwind to revenue growth than in Q2. Recent growth data are strong and earnings revision breadth remains positive.
Tariff refunds totaled $77 billion in Q2 and $69 billion in Q3, roughly 6% of total US corporate pre-tax profits each quarter. The earnings distortion from private equity stakes should fade in Q3.
Semis 3Q preview: GS sees upside to estimates across most sub-sectors after SOX fell 11% vs SPX up 4% over two months, which GS calls a more constructive setup than ahead of 2Q.

GS expects significant positive estimate revisions for SemiCap on pull-ins to WFE spending and visibility into 2028. In compute, it sees upside for server CPUs and key ASIC programs on higher hyperscaler capex.
GS is favorable on analog, preferring names with the greatest industrial, aero/defense and datacenter exposure. In memory/storage it prefers HDDs and NAND because of no near-term supply additions.
Banks 3Q preview: 3Q26 equities trading is expected to normalize QoQ, FICC is weak given the move in rates, and investment banking is much slower QoQ but still up YoY.

Banks: NII outlook rests on strong loan growth and fixed-rate asset repricing, partly offset by higher deposit costs. Capital deployment is expected to moderate on lower excess capital, AOCI impact from higher rates and three consecutive years of G-SIB buffer increases.

Bank valuation: shares fell 5% in 3Q26 on multiple derating. The average FY+2 P/E is at about the 50th percentile and the group trades at 60% of the S&P 500 multiple, 1pp below the historical level. A re-rating depends on clarity on the macro and the shape of the rates curve.
GS names WFC (on its Conviction List), BAC and C as the best positioned and most topical bank stocks.
Boeing: union contract ratification, the FAA declaring the 737 MAX software issue not a flight-safety risk, and the F/A-XX award are positives. GS is Buy rated.
Market update: NDX hit a new all-time high but rates, which backed up to pre-softer-NFP levels, limited risk appetite. Desk sees few buyers of duration.
Asset manager and HF flows were balanced on the week, with Semis demand rising after solid MU earnings and NVDA's increased buyback plans.

The S&P is down seven straight weeks per the desk, which it attributes to concentration into Tech at the expense of other sectors. Positioning is light but there is minimal willingness to chase the move higher.
Activity is spotty given performance challenges, an increasingly demanding macro backdrop (oil, rates), the midterm overhang and fast narrative shifts within AI.

market_movers.rationale: Union contract ratification reduces 777X timeline risk, the FAA cleared the 737 MAX software issue, and the F/A-XX award with F-47 supports the long-term defense growth outlook.

sector_views.rationale: Upside to 3Q estimates across most sub-sectors after a de-risking pullback. Prefers SemiCap, server CPUs, ASICs, analog, HDDs and NAND.
Valuation appears fair after a 5% decline in 3Q26. A re-rating needs macro and rates curve clarity, though ROTCEs stay attractive.
F/A-XX paired with F-47 bolsters the long-term growth outlook for Boeing's defense business.
